cases.explain: The word is the subject of the verb «молчал», and the subject of a sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я вынул из ___ все, что имею.
cases.translation: I took out of my little suitcase everything I own.
cases.explain: The preposition «из» ('out of') always governs the genitive: из чемоданчика.

cases.sentence: Нельзя же доверять ___ человека, который еще не успел похмелиться!
cases.translation: You really cannot trust the opinion of a man who has not yet managed to have his morning drink!
cases.explain: The verb «доверять» ('to trust') takes its object in the dative, so мнение becomes мнению.

cases.sentence: Я взял четвертинку и вышел в ___.
cases.translation: I took the quarter-bottle and went out into the vestibule of the carriage.
cases.explain: «В» answering «куда?» (movement into a place) requires the accusative; тамбур is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.translation: They all consider me a bad man.
cases.explain: «Считать кого-то кем-то» ('to consider someone something') puts the predicate noun in the instrumental: дурным человеком.

cases.sentence: Мой дух томился в ___ четыре с половиной часа.
cases.translation: My spirit languished in confinement for four and a half hours.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (a state or location, not direction) requires the prepositional: в заключении.

cases.translation: Share the meal with me, Lord!
cases.explain: «Трапеза» is the direct object of the transitive verb «раздели», and direct objects take the accusative.

reading.ru: Ну, конечно, все они считают меня дурным человеком.
reading.question: What does Venichka say other people think of him?
options: That he is a bad man
That he is a great poet
That he is a harmless drunk
That he is the cleverest man on the train
reading.correct: That he is a bad man
reading.explain: He opens the passage by admitting that everyone considers him a bad man.

reading.ru: По утрам и с перепою я сам о себе такого же мнения.
reading.question: When does Venichka himself share that opinion of himself?
options: In the mornings and when hung over
Only when he is completely sober
Whenever he is alone in the carriage
reading.correct: In the mornings and when hung over
reading.explain: He agrees with the bad opinion of himself only in the mornings and with a hangover; by evening he is full of abysses.

reading.ru: Утром плохо, а вечером хорошо – верный признак дурного человека.
reading.question: According to Venichka, what is a sure sign of a bad man?
options: Feeling wretched in the morning and fine in the evening
reading.correct: Feeling wretched in the morning and fine in the evening
reading.explain: He states this as a reliable sign, and applies it to himself.

reading.question: How does Venichka judge the man who is brisk and hopeful in the morning but exhausted by evening?
options: He says such a man does not exist
reading.explain: That type he calls trash, a wheeler-dealer and a mediocrity, and says he finds him repulsive.

reading.question: What question does Venichka ask himself before going through his belongings?
options: So then, what do I have?
So then, where am I going?
So then, when do the shops open?
reading.correct: So then, what do I have?
reading.explain: He asks what he has, and then empties the little suitcase to take stock of it.

reading.question: How does Venichka react after feeling over everything he owns?
options: He is suddenly seized by anguish
He is delighted with his supplies
He decides to give it all away
reading.correct: He is suddenly seized by anguish
reading.explain: Handling his goods — from the sandwich to the pink fortified wine — leaves him anguished and faded rather than pleased.

reading.question: What does the Lord say about St Teresa's stigmata?
options: She does not need them, but they are desired by her
She needs them in order to be a saint
They were given to her as a punishment
reading.correct: She does not need them, but they are desired by her
reading.explain: God answers that the stigmata are not needed by Teresa either, yet they are desired — the same as Venichka's bottle.

reading.question: What happens while Venichka waits to hear whether God will say anything more?
options: God tells him to get off the train
God repeats the answer about the stigmata
reading.explain: He hesitates, waiting for more, but the Lord stays silent.

reading.ru: Я взял четвертинку и вышел в тамбур.
reading.question: Where does Venichka go with the quarter-bottle?
options: Out into the vestibule of the carriage
Out onto the platform at Serp i Molot
Back to his seat by the window
reading.correct: Out into the vestibule of the carriage
reading.explain: He takes the quarter-bottle and steps out into the tambur (the vestibule between carriages) to drink.

reading.ru: Мой дух томился в заключении четыре с половиной часа, теперь я выпущу его погулять.
reading.question: How long does Venichka say his spirit has been held in confinement?
reading.explain: He says his spirit has languished in confinement for four and a half hours and that he will now let it out for a walk.

reading.ru: Есть стакан и есть бутерброд, чтобы не стошнило.
reading.question: Why does Venichka mention having a sandwich?
options: So that he will not be sick
Because he has not eaten for days
To share it with a fellow passenger
To trade it for another drink
reading.correct: So that he will not be sick
reading.explain: The sandwich is there purely as a chaser, to stop him from feeling sick after the drink.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that you cannot trust the judgement of a man who has not yet had his morning drink?
sentences: Ну, конечно, все они считают меня дурным человеком.
По утрам и с перепою я сам о себе такого же мнения.
Но ведь нельзя же доверять мнению человека, который еще не успел похмелиться!
Зато по вечерам – какие во мне бездны! – если, конечно, хорошо набраться за день, – какие бездны во мне по вечерам!
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the one that dismisses the opinion of an unhungover man as untrustworthy.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the reason the shops' closing times matter for not being a scoundrel?
sentences: Конечно, бывают и такие, кому одинаково любо и утром, и вечером, и восходу они рады, и закату тоже рады, – так это уж просто мерзавцы, о них и говорить-то противно.
Ну уж, а если кому одинаково скверно – и утром, и вечером – тут уж я не знаю, что и сказать, это уж конченный подонок и мудозвон.
Потому что магазины у нас работают до девяти, а Елисеевский – тот даже до одиннадцати, и если ты не подонок, ты всегда сумеешь к вечеру подняться до чего-нибудь, до какой-нибудь пустяшной бездны…
highlight.explain: The last sentence explains that since the shops stay open until nine (and Yeliseyevsky until eleven), anyone who is not a scoundrel can rise to some small abyss by evening.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that St Teresa desires the stigmata even so?
sentences: – А для чего нужны стигматы святой Терезе?
Они ведь ей тоже не нужны.
highlight.explain: The final sentence is the one about the stigmata being desired, not needed.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells us how long Venichka's spirit has been shut up?
sentences: Я взял четвертинку и вышел в тамбур.
Мой дух томился в заключении четыре с половиной часа, теперь я выпущу его погулять.
Есть стакан и есть бутерброд, чтобы не стошнило.
И есть душа, пока еще чуть приоткрытая для впечатлений бытия.
highlight.explain: Only the fourth sentence gives the length of time — four and a half hours.
